sources.title: Climbing in Chulilla
sources.notes: Local Valencia climbing operator; used for limestone canyon, sport routes, grades, season, accommodation and village access notes.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.body: Chulilla is a Valencia-region limestone canyon climbing destination focused on long sport routes.

sections.heading: History and context
warnings: No sourced history and context content found for this pass.

sections.heading: Rock and climbing character
sections.body: The climbing is on orange and grey limestone walls in the Turia river canyon, with sustained sport routes, tufas, pockets and crimpy wall climbing.

sections.heading: Who it suits
sections.body: The area is useful for sport climbers seeking endurance mileage across moderate to hard grades rather than a single roadside crag experience.

sections.heading: Grades and difficulty
sections.body: Valencia Climb gives the grade span as 5 to 8c+.

sections.heading: Season and conditions
sections.body: Winter is a common visiting season; the canyon has varied orientations for sun or shade. Summer heat is an avoid condition rather than a target season.

sections.heading: Gear and equipment
warnings: No sourced gear and equipment content found for this pass.

sections.heading: Transport and access
sections.body: Valencia is the nearest normalized airport city. A car is useful for area logistics, although some village-based access is practical once in Chulilla.

sections.heading: Where to stay
sections.body: The village has a climbers refuge and flats; nearby villages are used when high-season beds fill.

sections.heading: Rest days
warnings: No sourced rest days content found for this pass.

sections.heading: Practical tips
sections.body: High-season crowding is specifically called out around Christmas and Easter holidays.

sections.heading: Safety notes
sections.body: Local notes warn that popular routes may be polished; route choice should account for grade, aspect, and crowding.
